feed.title: Zhang Lab
feed.subtitle: Here in the Worm lab, we study the neurobiology of homeostasis where we have a special interest in body fluid balance and cilia diseases. Using multidisciplinary approaches, new tools, and developing novel protocol, we strive to anser the most exciting scientific questions!

entry.title: Welcome Kaiser!
entry.content:
The Zhang Lab is excited to extend a belated but warm welcome to Kaiser! Kaiser is an academically outstanding high school student with a strong passion for science. This year, he joined our lab through a research program to gain hands-on experience in scientific research, exploring Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) and the functions of its sensory neurons.

We are delighted to have Kaiser as part of our team and look forward to seeing his curiosity and enthusiasm for science grow. It is truly a pleasure to get to know this promising “future scientist”!

entry.title: Zhang Lab Receives NIH Research Funding!

link.title: Zhang Lab Receives NIH Research Funding!

entry.content:
We are thrilled to share that the Zhang Lab has received research funding from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to support our project, “Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms of Fluid Balance in C. elegans” (Grant No. 1R35GM162254-01), led by Dr. Xinxing Zhang.

This funding will support our efforts to uncover the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying fluid balance using Caenorhabditis elegans as a model organism, advancing our understanding of this fundamental biological process.

We are deeply grateful to the NIH for its generous support and recognition of our research. This award represents an exciting milestone for our lab and provides a wonderful opportunity to pursue new discoveries.

entry.title: Cell bio symposium!
entry.content:
From October 28–30, 2026, members of the Zhang Lab attended the Cell Biology Symposium, enjoying three days of inspiring scientific presentations, engaging discussions, and exciting discoveries.

A special congratulations to Dr. Xinxing Zhang on delivering an excellent presentation! His talk sparked great interest and lively discussions among the attendees. We are so proud of him!

Throughout the symposium, we had the opportunity to learn about a wide range of fascinating research topics, exchange ideas with fellow scientists, and gain valuable new insights.

It was a wonderful experience filled with learning and inspiration. We look forward to more opportunities to connect, learn, and grow together as a team!

entry.title: Welcome Thalia!
entry.content:
The Zhang Lab is delighted to welcome Thalia Avila as a summer student researcher! Originally from Peru, Thalia is currently a Biology major at the University of Oklahoma with a strong interest in cell biology, bioinformatics, and the exciting intersection of science and technology. Her enthusiasm for scientific discovery and eagerness to learn make her a wonderful addition to the lab this summer.

Outside of academics, Thalia enjoys traveling, experiencing new cultures, and trying new things, reflecting the curiosity and adventurous mindset that she brings to research as well. We are excited to have her join the Zhang Lab and look forward to working with her on new scientific experiences and discoveries throughout the summer. Welcome, Thalia!

entry.title: Zhang Lab Receives Support from NIH COBRE program!

link.title: Zhang Lab Receives Support from NIH COBRE program!

entry.content:
We are excited to share that the Zhang Lab has received support from the NIH COBRE program for a new research project focused on understanding copper-sensing mechanisms in Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans). This funding, awarded on May 5, 2026, will help our lab investigate how organisms detect and respond to changes in copper levels, an essential process for maintaining cellular health and survival.

We sincerely thank the NIH COBRE program for its support and confidence in our research！

entry.title: Inspiring Future Scientists at Red Oak Elementary!

link.title: Inspiring Future Scientists at Red Oak Elementary!

entry.content:
Red Oak Elementary’s STEM Night was a wonderful evening filled with curiosity, creativity, and hands-on learning for students and families alike. As one of the volunteer groups participating in the event, the Zhang Lab was excited to introduce students to Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans), a tiny roundworm widely used as a model organism in scientific research. Through fun and interactive activities—including coloring pages, trivia games with prizes, 3D puzzle building, and live microscope observations—students learned about the worm’s appearance, life cycle, and importance in biological research while exploring science in an engaging way.

We are especially grateful to Dr. Lurdes Queimado and her team for their generous support and assistance throughout the event. Their dedication and hard work played an essential role in making the evening such a great success. We loved sharing the excitement of science with the community and hope the event inspired many future young scientists!

entry.title: Shining Bright Together!
entry.content:
The weather may be getting colder, but the Zhang Lab’s warmth and energy are as strong as ever!

We recently took a lovely group photo against a beautiful backdrop — a perfect reminder that even as the seasons change, our team spirit shines bright.

Just like the stars we posed as in the photo, we hope everyone in the lab continues to sparkle in their own way — whether it’s through new discoveries, creative ideas, or the laughter we share every day.
